item.title: Harry and Meghan Are Already Annoying British Taxpayers
item.description: Six years on from their dramatic UK departure, Prince Harry and his wife Meghan are returning from California with their two small children. Royal watchers have many questions: Where will they live and where will Archie and Lilibet go to school? What does this say about Harry’s strained relationship with his father King Charles and brother William? And can Meghan forgive William’s wife Catherine after they fell out over whether the latter’s daughter wore tights to Harry’s wedding?
item.dc:creator: Rosa Prince

item.title: AI Models: Nvidia Is Jolting Silicon Valley to Think Like China
item.description: When a typical business finds its supply chain costs have risen, it will absorb the increase to keep its customers happy. Nvidia isn’t a typical business. It enjoys gross profit margins of 75% and commands between 70% and 90% of the global market for artificial-intelligence chips. So when the companies that make memory components put their prices up, Nvidia passed the hike on. item.title: Ambani’s Succession Plan Confronts a Wildlife Problem
item.description: Asia’s second-richest business clan just made a highly public commitment to rein in its youngest scion’s passion project, a controversial wildlife sanctuary. In doing so, tycoon Mukesh Ambani is cutting the risks to his empire and ironing out a major wrinkle in his succession plans.

item.title: Luxury Should Embrace China’s Secondhand Boom
item.description: With a 20-year spending spree over, luxury brands must reinvent the way they relate to Chinese consumers. There’s no better way to do that than by embracing the country’s flourishing secondhand market.
item.dc:creator: Juliana Liu

item.title: Gary, Indiana’s Suffering in a Blackout Brings a Global Crisis Home
item.description: After a small city with a struggling economy is slammed by hurricane-force winds, thousands of its people go weeks without electricity. They grow increasingly desperate as they run out of food, medicine and money. This just happened, not in a foreign country, not even in a chronically neglected US territory like Puerto Rico, but in Gary, Indiana, right in America’s heartland.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gongloff

item.description: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Teens, complete with various safety features. But this implies that the main concern of kids using AI is their access to damaging content. If only.

item.title: Burnham Isn’t Ready For How Much Russia Hates the UK
item.description: In the current Russian leadership’s rather 19th — though increasingly 21st — century view of how the world works, lesser powers must defer to great ones or pay the price. The UK, a country in a category all of its own when it comes to Kremlin resentments, has just been warned that it’s in line for such a punishment and I’m not sure that’s being taken seriously enough.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: Quantum Computing: The Race to 100 Error-Corrected Qubits Is Defining Progress
item.description: When the Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer, or Eniac, was first built by the University of Pennsylvania for the US Army in 1946, it weighed about 30 tons and had 18,000 vacuum tubes that filled an expansive room. The speed of that first programmable, general-purpose digital computer was about 5,000 hertz, which means it could perform 5,000 additions per second. It cost about $9 million to build in today’s dollars.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Black

item.title: US Unemployment Rate Would Be Less Representative With Private Data
item.description: The logic seems straightforward enough: To make its decisions, the Federal Reserve needs timely and reliable information. A lot of that is public, but increasingly, there is relevant data in private hands. Ergo, the Fed should use these new sources to help the bank be more forward-looking.
item.dc:creator: Kathryn Anne Edwards
